description: Search and list SEC filings by company (CIK), form type, date range, 8-K item codes and excluded forms, optionally with a full-text query over filing bodies, and optionally by COMPANY FACTS (market cap, float, price, sector, industry, exchange, company type, foreign issuer, recent IPO). Returns rows with `id` (the filingId for get_filing_document / get_filing_exhibits), cik, company_name, accession_number, form_type, filing_date, acceptedAt, primaryDocument, bodyStored and itemNumbers, plus `pagination` with `total`, `totalRelation` ("eq" exact; "gte" a lower bound when the count was cut at 10,000 — then `totalEstimate`, when present, is "about N"), `hasMore` and `nextCursor`. With `q`, unfiltered rows also carry `rank` and a `snippet`. Coverage: Signal8's archive of SEC EDGAR filings in the archive's held range (see `archiveFrom` in each response; currently from late 2021, expanding back to 2016 as the history backfill fills in), updated through the day. The archive only holds filings from its `archiveFrom` date; before that it holds only a scatter (well under 1% of most years), so ABSENCE BEFORE archiveFrom IS NOT EVIDENCE a filing was never filed — check SEC EDGAR for earlier periods. Some rows are record-only (bodyStored: false — metadata from the EDGAR index with no document body), so their text cannot be read here; open them at their sec.gov URL. Full-text `q`: Query syntax: unquoted words must ALL appear (any order, any distance); "quoted phrase" = exact wording; OR between alternatives (merger OR acquisition); -word or -"phrase" to exclude; w1 NEAR/10 w2 (also NEAR(10), or bare NEAR = within 10) = words close together; word* = prefix of 4+ letters (dilut* matches dilution, dilutive); $AAPL or a capitalised ticker scopes to that company; a form code (8-K, 10-Q, S-1), "item 5.02" / "8-K 1.05" and a bare year (2024) scope to that form / 8-K item / year. The archive's reading of the query (tickers/companies, forms, items, years, synonym expansions such as buyback → share repurchase) is returned in `meta.understanding` when stated; pass understand=false to search the words literally. Pass facets=true for `facets` — counts of matching filings per form type, per year and per 8-K item over the WHOLE result set (absent when not measured, e.g. on the Postgres engine — never read absence as zero). With sort=relevance, page 1 shows at most a few filings per company; meta.diversity { maxPerCompany, hidden: [{cik, count}] } names who has more — page on with nextCursor (not page) or filter by that CIK. SECTION SEARCH: section=risk_factors (or mdna, business, ex99 for press releases, item_5_02, …) restricts matching to those sections; rows then carry matchedSections and meta.sections confirms it — if meta.unsupported names section instead, the whole filing was searched. exhibitTypes=EX-10 keeps filings with a material contract (EX-99.1 press release, EX-97 clawback, …); facets=true adds facets.sections / facets.exhibitTypes when measured. An empty text result is only definitive when the response's `searchIndex.complete` is true — otherwise `notes` says the index has not confirmed full coverage of the range. Every response carries `archiveFrom` and `rangeStartsBeforeArchive`: a range with no dateFrom, or starting before archiveFrom, is NEVER definitive (`searchIndex.complete: false`, `reason: "outside_held_range"`, `heldFrom`) and `notes` says so — report "the archive only holds filings from <archiveFrom>; absence before that is not evidence", never "no such filing exists". Pass a dateFrom on or after archiveFrom for a definitive empty answer. The `ciks` filter matches the filing's own CIK: an insider Form 4 filed under the reporting owner's CIK is NOT returned for the issuer's CIK. COMPANY FILTERS (any of minMarketCap … recentIpo) are served from the archive only, using Signal8's company data: (1) only issuer-filed forms are searched (10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, S-1, S-3, 424B*, DEF 14A, 20-F, 6-K, …); third-party forms such as Form 4, 144 and SCHEDULE 13D/G are dropped and listed in `companyFilter.droppedForms` — unless `companyFilter.subjectMatch` is true, in which case they ARE searched, matched by the company they are about — and with no formTypes the default is 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, S-1, S-3, DEF 14A, 20-F, 40-F, 6-K; (2) companies with no measured value for a filter are EXCLUDED, never assumed, and `companyFilter.unknown` counts them per filter; (3) unknown values (e.g. a misspelt sector) are a 400 that lists the allowed names; (4) when the archive cannot answer (e.g. a date range it does not fully hold yet) the call FAILS with code COMPANY_FILTER_NOT_APPLIED and a reason — it never returns unfiltered rows; (5) results are cursor-paged (use nextCursor, not page) and cannot be combined with acceptedFrom/acceptedTo/bodyStored; company-filtered text matches carry no snippet (use search_filing_text with the accessionNumber for the excerpt). The response then includes `companyFilter` (matchedCompanies, searchedCompanies, unknown, forms, droppedForms), `appliedFilters` and `notes`. To COUNT or list companies (not filings) by market cap etc., use screen_companies instead.

ciks.description: Comma-separated CIK numbers to filter by (e.g., "320193,1018724"; zero-padded also accepted)

companyTypes.description: COMPANY FILTER. Comma-separated: operating, fund (registered funds/ETFs; adds N-CSR, N-CEN, N-PX, 485BPOS, 497/497K to the default forms), spac (blank-check companies)

cursor.description: Opaque keyset cursor from a previous response's pagination.nextCursor. Prefer it over page for deep paging — it is stable while new filings arrive. Required for page 2+ of a company-filtered search.

dateFrom.description: Start filing date (YYYY-MM-DD). The archive only holds filings from its `archiveFrom` date (stated in every response; currently late 2021, expanding back to 2016): omitting dateFrom, or starting earlier, makes an empty result non-definitive.

exchanges.description: COMPANY FILTER. Comma-separated listing venues: NASDAQ, NYSE, AMEX (= NYSE American), OTC

excludeForms.description: Comma-separated form types to EXCLUDE (e.g., "4,13F-HR"). Exact match.

exhibitTypes.description: Keep only filings carrying ANY of these exhibit types (comma-separated): a family such as EX-10 (material contracts) matches every member (EX-10.1, EX-10.2…); an exact type such as EX-99.1 (usually the press release) only itself. Others: EX-97 clawback policy, EX-3 charter/bylaws, EX-4 instruments/warrants, EX-21 subsidiaries, EX-23 consents. "10.1" is accepted for EX-10.1. Listed in appliedFilters when the rows prove it; otherwise in ignoredFilters / meta.unsupported — treat the rows as unfiltered then.

facets.description: true = also return `facets`: { forms, years, items }, each a list of { value, count } over the WHOLE result set (not just this page). Present only when the archive measured them (its OpenSearch engine); absent means NOT MEASURED, never zero. Default false.

foreignIssuer.description: COMPANY FILTER. true = companies with foreign-issuer evidence (a 20-F, 40-F or 6-K seen, or an ADR listing); false = none seen since the evidence log began (companyFilter.foreignEvidenceSince)

formTypes.description: Comma-separated form types (e.g., "10-K,10-Q,8-K,S-1,S-3,424B5"). Exact match — list amendments (e.g. "10-K/A") explicitly. (With company filters, amendments are added automatically.)

industries.description: COMPANY FILTER. Industry names separated by "|", exact and case-sensitive (e.g. "Biotechnology|Airlines, Airports & Air Services" — some names contain ", ", so prefer "|"; a bare comma with no space after it also separates). An unknown name returns a 400 listing every valid industry.

items.description: Comma-separated 8-K item codes, ALL required (e.g., "2.02,9.01" = results + financial statements; "5.02" = officer/director changes; "1.01" = material agreements; "3.01" = delisting notice).

match.description: Word matching for q. exact = a word matches only itself ("split" does NOT match "splits" or "splitting") — EDGAR full-text search's own behaviour; stemmed = English word variations also match. Default when omitted: stemmed. The mode actually APPLIED is in the response's meta.matchMode (with meta.matchModeFallbackReason when it differs from the one asked for); meta.engine names the search engine. Ignored without q.

matchedSections.description: Per-row `matchedSections` (default true): the sections the text matched in. ABSENT on a row means not measured (index without sections), never "matched nowhere". Ignored without q.

maxFloat.description: COMPANY FILTER. Maximum public float, in SHARES

maxMarketCap.description: COMPANY FILTER. Maximum market cap in USD, e.g. 300000000 for under $300M

maxPrice.description: COMPANY FILTER. Maximum latest share price in USD

minFloat.description: COMPANY FILTER. Minimum public float, in SHARES

minMarketCap.description: COMPANY FILTER. Minimum market cap in USD (price × shares outstanding), e.g. 50000000 for $50M

minPrice.description: COMPANY FILTER. Minimum latest share price in USD

page.description: Page number (1-indexed, default: 1). Ignored when cursor is set; not allowed with company filters.

q.description: Full-text query over filing bodies. Query syntax: unquoted words must ALL appear (any order, any distance); "quoted phrase" = exact wording; OR between alternatives (merger OR acquisition); -word or -"phrase" to exclude; w1 NEAR/10 w2 (also NEAR(10), or bare NEAR = within 10) = words close together; word* = prefix of 4+ letters (dilut* matches dilution, dilutive); $AAPL or a capitalised ticker scopes to that company; a form code (8-K, 10-Q, S-1), "item 5.02" / "8-K 1.05" and a bare year (2024) scope to that form / 8-K item / year. Example: '$AAPL "share repurchase" -"no longer"', 'cyber* NEAR/10 incident', 'item 5.02 resign*'.

recentIpo.description: COMPANY FILTER. true = first listed within the last 365 days, with no evidence of earlier public status (renames and relistings are excluded). false is the same as omitting it.

section.description: Restrict MATCHING to sections (comma-separated): business, risk_factors, cybersecurity, legal_proceedings, mdna, market_risk, controls (10-K/10-Q/20-F narrative items, by meaning — mdna is 10-K Item 7, 10-Q Part I Item 2 and 20-F Item 5), ex99 (press-release / EX-99.x exhibit text) and item_X_YY (the text under an 8-K item, e.g. item_5_02). Aliases: mda, risk, legal, cyber, press_release, 5.02. Unknown names are a 400. Needs q. Applied ONLY when the response's meta.sections names it — otherwise meta.unsupported says why (e.g. the archive index does not have sections yet) and matches may come from ANYWHERE in the filing.

sectors.description: COMPANY FILTER. Sector names separated by "|" (or a bare comma), exact and case-sensitive (e.g. "Healthcare|Technology"). An unknown name returns a 400 listing every valid sector.

sort.description: newest (by acceptance time, default) or relevance (requires q; best match first)

understand.description: Query understanding (default true): the archive recognises tickers/$TICKER, company names, form codes, "item N.NN" and expands synonyms, reporting what it applied in meta.understanding. false = search the words literally (also disables synonym expansion). Ignored without q.

name: search_sec_filings
title: Search SEC Filings
